meta.title: About SignageWall
meta.description: Why we built SignageWall: signage software with one price, every feature included, and a player designed to keep running when the network does not.

hero.title: Screens should be the boring part of your day.
hero.subtitle: Not a thing you check on. Not a thing that needs a technician. SignageWall exists because signage software kept getting that backwards.

story.title: Why we built it.
paragraphs: We kept walking into the same room. A screen switched off, or frozen on an image from last spring, or showing an error nobody had noticed for a week. Not because the business did not care — because changing it meant remembering a password, opening a tool built for someone else, and finding that the thing you wanted was in a plan you had not bought.

So the product is shaped around two ideas. The price is one number with everything switched on, because a feature matrix is just a way of charging you twice. And the player assumes the network will fail, because it will: it keeps a local copy, plays through the outage, and restarts itself if it ever stalls.

build.title: The parts we spent the most time on.
build.subtitle: Not the parts that demo well — the parts that decide whether a screen is still right in six months.

items.title: Offline first, not offline-tolerant
items.body: The player downloads and stores content, then plays from disk. The network is how content arrives, never how it plays. A dropped connection is invisible to anyone standing in front of the screen.

items.title: A watchdog that does not wait for you
items.body: A separate process checks that the player is not just running but actually drawing frames, and restarts it if it stalls. Most signage outages are not crashes — they are a frozen picture nobody reports for days.

items.title: Updates that cannot brick a screen
items.body: Players update themselves over the air, verify what they downloaded before switching to it, and roll back if the new version does not come up healthy. A screen in a shop window is not somewhere you want a failed update.

items.title: One price, held to
items.body: Every feature is on for every account. There is no plan matrix to maintain, which also means there is no incentive for us to move something you rely on into a higher tier next year.

items.title: Simple wins
items.body: If it needs explaining, it is not finished. Anyone who can post to social media should be able to run a screen without training.

items.title: Reliable beats featureful
items.body: A frozen screen is worse than a blank one. We would rather ship fewer things that never need checking on.

items.title: Say the price
items.body: Published, at every size. If you have to ask what software costs, the answer is usually that it depends on how much they think you can pay.

items.title: No watermark, ever
items.body: Not on a trial, not on any plan. Your screen advertises your business, not our software.

contact.title: Talk to us.
contact.body: Questions about how it works, whether it fits, or what it would cost for your network — we answer within one business day.
